name: Mixmaster Chaotic Cosmology
description: A spatially homogeneous Bianchi type IX cosmology whose approach to the singularity consists of an infinite, chaotic sequence of Kasner oscillations. It is the prototype of chaotic cosmological dynamics near a singularity.
convention: Coordinates are $(t, \psi, \theta, \phi)$ with $t$ a cosmic time and $\psi$, $\theta$ and $\phi$ Euler angles on a three sphere, $\psi \in [0, 4\pi)$, $\theta \in [0, \pi]$ and $\phi \in [0, 2\pi)$, and factors of $c$ are kept explicit. Each slice of constant $t$ is closed, and the line element is written in the three one forms that the symmetry of the slice leaves unchanged, $\omega^1 = \cos\psi\,d\theta + \sin\psi\sin\theta\,d\phi$, $\omega^2 = \sin\psi\,d\theta - \cos\psi\sin\theta\,d\phi$ and $\omega^3 = d\psi + \cos\theta\,d\phi$, as $ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + a_1^2(\omega^1)^2 + a_2^2(\omega^2)^2 + a_3^2(\omega^3)^2$. They obey $d\omega^1 = \omega^2\wedge\omega^3$ and its two cyclic partners, which is what makes the slices type IX in Bianchi's list, the type whose group is that of rotations. This is the form Misner wrote in 1969 and Belinskii, Khalatnikov and Lifshitz in 1970, with their $a$, $b$ and $c$ written $a_1$, $a_2$ and $a_3$; Misner's variables are the logarithms, $a_1 = e^{\alpha + \beta_+ + \sqrt{3}\beta_-}$, $a_2 = e^{\alpha + \beta_+ - \sqrt{3}\beta_-}$ and $a_3 = e^{\alpha - 2\beta_+}$, with $e^{\alpha}$ carrying the length. The three scale factors are left free functions of $t$ and are lengths, since the angles carry none. Where all three equal $a$ the slice is a round three sphere of radius $2a$ and the metric is closed Friedmann, and where two agree the slices keep a further rotation about the third direction, the symmetry of Taub's vacuum solution of 1951. In the coordinate basis the components carry $\psi$ only because $\omega^1$ and $\omega^2$ turn with it; the geometry is the same at every point of a slice. Components are taken in the chart $x^0 = ct$, where a chart component of the metric carries no dimensions. A prime is the derivative along that chart time, $a_i' = da_i/d(ct)$, so $a_i'$ is dimensionless and $a_i''$ carries an inverse length, and the dots in the geodesic equations are velocities of the same chart, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$. The signature is $(-,+,+,+)$ and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$, which the Ricci scalar and the Einstein tensor follow.¶No component assumes a field equation. Every component is an identity for any three scale factors, and the Mixmaster is the vacuum among them. In the frame $c\,dt$, $a_1\omega^1$, $a_2\omega^2$ and $a_3\omega^3$ the Ricci tensor is diagonal, and the vacuum equations read $\dfrac{\left(a_1'a_2a_3\right)'}{a_1a_2a_3} = \dfrac{\left(a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)^2 - a_1^4}{2a_1^2a_2^2a_3^2}$ with its two cyclic partners, together with the constraint $G^t{}_t = 0$, $\dfrac{a_1'a_2'}{a_1a_2} + \dfrac{a_1'a_3'}{a_1a_3} + \dfrac{a_2'a_3'}{a_2a_3} = \dfrac{a_1^4 + a_2^4 + a_3^4 - 2a_1^2a_2^2 - 2a_1^2a_3^2 - 2a_2^2a_3^2}{4a_1^2a_2^2a_3^2}$. Drop the right hand sides and these are the Kasner equations, whose solutions are the Kasner epochs; the right hand sides are the curvature of the closed slice, the walls of Misner's billiard, negligible while one scale factor is much larger than the other two and decisive when the growing one catches them, which is the bounce that deals out the next set of exponents. The line element can be written down whatever the solution does; the chaos is in the solutions of these equations, not in the metric that carries them.
history: Charles Misner wanted the smoothness of the universe earned rather than assumed. The microwave background arrives at one temperature from patches of sky that never exchanged a signal, and by 1968 he had his answer, a program he called chaotic cosmology [misner1968]: let the young universe be as lopsided as it likes, then find the dynamics that grind it smooth. In 1969 he took up the closed anisotropic vacuum of Bianchi type IX and named it the Mixmaster, after the Sunbeam kitchen mixer, expecting it to stir the early universe smooth [misner1969]. Toward the singularity it runs through Kasner epochs, the axis with the one negative exponent running away while the other two crush, until the curvature of the closed slices deals the exponents out again. There is no last bounce, and infinitely many fit into the finite proper time that remains.¶Evgeny Lifshitz and Isaak Khalatnikov reached the same oscillation in Moscow from the other direction, at the cost of seven years of work. They had argued in 1963 that the general solution of the Einstein equations carries no singularity, the known ones being a penalty of symmetry [lifshitz1963]. Penrose's theorem of 1965 made that position uninhabitable [penrose1965]. With Vladimir Belinskii they went back and in 1970 published retraction and replacement together: a general solution that does reach a singularity, through Mixmaster oscillations [khalatnikov1970, bkl1970]. The replacement was the bolder claim. Near a spacelike singularity the time derivatives drown out the spatial ones, so every point of a generic spacetime collapses on its own private Bianchi IX schedule, set by one number that sheds a unit at each bounce until it drops below one, whereupon the next era opens at its reciprocal.¶Misner's own formulation made it visible: take the volume as the clock and the shape as a point with two coordinates, and Bianchi IX becomes one particle in a potential well shaped like an equilateral triangle with an open channel at each corner. Rescale until the walls hold still and harden into mirrors, and the universe is a billiard ball on a surface of constant negative curvature, the classic mixing system. It sat unpublished in a 1972 Maryland thesis by D. M. Chitre until Misner wrote it up for him twenty two years later, in a volume pointedly titled Deterministic Chaos in General Relativity [misner1994].¶By then the model had failed its own purpose: the oscillations do not mix the sky into causal contact [doroshkevich1971], and the horizon problem waited for inflation [guth1981]. John Barrow gave the bounce map a positive Lyapunov exponent in 1982 [barrow1982], but an exponent measures separation per unit of time and relativity supplies no preferred unit: change the clock and other coordinates return zero [francisco1988, berger1991]. Neil Cornish and Janna Levin ended a decade of argument in 1997 by declining to measure time at all: the phase space carries a fractal, and a fractal does not care what clock you hold [cornish1997]. Adilson Motter settled the principle in 2003: positive Lyapunov exponents stay positive under a change of coordinates [motter2003].¶Misner's billiard reaches beyond four dimensions. Pure gravity stops bouncing in eleven spacetime dimensions and above [demaret1985], awkwardly, since eleven is where supergravity lives; restore its three form field and the walls come back, the table now the Weyl chamber of the hyperbolic Kac-Moody algebra $E_{10}$ [damour2003]. The appliance Misner named in 1969 is the shape of the singularity in M-theory.

coordinates.name: Euler Angles

parameters.description: Scale factor along the first invariant direction of the three sphere, a length, positive; its direction $\cos\psi\,d\theta + \sin\psi\sin\theta\,d\phi$ turns with $\psi$, which is why $\psi$ appears in the components at all. A prime is the derivative along the chart time, $a_1' = da_1/d(ct)$, so $a_1'$ is dimensionless and $a_1''$ carries an inverse length
Scale factor along the second invariant direction, $\sin\psi\,d\theta - \cos\psi\sin\theta\,d\phi$, a length, positive

Scale factor along the third invariant direction, $d\psi + \cos\theta\,d\phi$, a length, positive; the three are independent, the model is Taub's where two of them agree and closed Friedmann, a three sphere of radius $2a$, where all three equal $a$

nonzero.value: \dfrac{\left(a_1^2\,a_2^2\left(\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\sin^2\psi - \left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 + a_3^2\right)\cos^2\psi\right)\sin^2\theta - a_3^2\left(a_1^2\cos^2\psi + a_2^2\sin^2\psi\right)\left(a_1^2 + a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\cos^2\theta\right)\csc\theta}{2a_1^2\,a_2^2\,a_3^2}

\dfrac{\left(a_1^2\,a_2^2\left(\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\sin^2\psi - \left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 + a_3^2\right)\cos^2\psi\right)\sin^2\theta - a_3^2\left(a_1^2\cos^2\psi + a_2^2\sin^2\psi\right)\left(a_1^2 + a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\cos^2\theta\right)\csc\theta}{2a_1^2\,a_2^2\,a_3^2}

geodesics: \ddot{\psi} + \dfrac{2a_3'}{a_3}\dot{t}\dot{\psi} + \dfrac{2\left(a_1\,a_2' - a_2\,a_1'\right)\sin\psi\cos\psi\cot\theta}{a_1\,a_2}\dot{t}\dot{\theta} + \dfrac{2\left(a_1\left(a_2\,a_3' - a_3\,a_2'\right)\cos^2\psi + a_2\left(a_1\,a_3' - a_3\,a_1'\right)\sin^2\psi\right)\cos\theta}{a_1\,a_2\,a_3}\dot{t}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{\left(a_2^2\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 + a_3^2\right)\sin^2\psi - a_1^2\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\cos^2\psi\right)\cot\theta}{a_1^2\,a_2^2}\dot{\psi}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2\right)\left(a_1^2 + a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\sin\psi\cos\psi\cos\theta}{a_1^2\,a_2^2}\dot{\psi}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2\right)\sin\psi\cos\psi}{a_3^2}\dot{\theta}^2 + \dfrac{\left(a_1^2\,a_2^2\left(\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\sin^2\psi - \left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 + a_3^2\right)\cos^2\psi\right)\sin^2\theta - a_3^2\left(a_1^2\cos^2\psi + a_2^2\sin^2\psi\right)\left(a_1^2 + a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\cos^2\theta\right)\csc\theta}{a_1^2\,a_2^2\,a_3^2}\dot{\theta}\dot{\phi} - \dfrac{\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2\right)\left(a_1^2\,a_2^2\sin^2\theta + a_3^2\left(a_1^2 + a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\cos^2\theta\right)\sin\psi\cos\psi}{a_1^2\,a_2^2\,a_3^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

\ddot{\theta} + \dfrac{2a_1\,a_2'\,\sin^2\psi + 2a_2\,a_1'\,\cos^2\psi}{a_1\,a_2}\dot{t}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{2\left(a_1\,a_2' - a_2\,a_1'\right)\sin\psi\cos\psi\sin\theta}{a_1\,a_2}\dot{t}\dot{\phi} - \dfrac{\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2\right)\left(a_1^2 + a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\sin\psi\cos\psi}{a_1^2\,a_2^2}\dot{\psi}\dot{\theta} + \dfrac{\left(a_2^2\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 + a_3^2\right)\cos^2\psi - a_1^2\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\sin^2\psi\right)\sin\theta}{a_1^2\,a_2^2}\dot{\psi}\dot{\phi} - \dfrac{\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2\right)\left(a_1^2 + a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\sin\psi\cos\psi\cos\theta}{a_1^2\,a_2^2}\dot{\theta}\dot{\phi} - \dfrac{\left(a_1^2\left(a_1^2 - a_3^2\right)\sin^2\psi + a_2^2\left(a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\cos^2\psi\right)\sin\theta\cos\theta}{a_1^2\,a_2^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

\ddot{\phi} - \dfrac{2\left(a_1\,a_2' - a_2\,a_1'\right)\sin\psi\cos\psi\csc\theta}{a_1\,a_2}\dot{t}\dot{\theta} + \dfrac{2a_1\,a_2'\,\cos^2\psi + 2a_2\,a_1'\,\sin^2\psi}{a_1\,a_2}\dot{t}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{\left(a_1^2\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\cos^2\psi - a_2^2\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2 + a_3^2\right)\sin^2\psi\right)\csc\theta}{a_1^2\,a_2^2}\dot{\psi}\dot{\theta} + \dfrac{\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2\right)\left(a_1^2 + a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\sin\psi\cos\psi}{a_1^2\,a_2^2}\dot{\psi}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{\left(a_1^2 + a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\left(a_1^2\cos^2\psi + a_2^2\sin^2\psi\right)\cot\theta}{a_1^2\,a_2^2}\dot{\theta}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{\left(a_1^2 - a_2^2\right)\left(a_1^2 + a_2^2 - a_3^2\right)\sin\psi\cos\psi\cos\theta}{a_1^2\,a_2^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0
